summary: Backend regression: 31/31 pytest PASS (test_auth_saas.py + test_phase1_features.py). Static code review of the WhatsApp PDF share fix (whatsapp.ts) confirms every requirement: (a) NO openWhatsAppChat deep-link call at start of shareQuoteViaWhatsApp on native — it is only invoked as a last-resort fallback when Sharing.isAvailableAsync()===false. (b) On native, pdfUri is copied (or moved if already in cache) into FileSystem.cacheDirectory as `${safeNo}.pdf` with teklifNo sanitised to `[A-Za-z0-9_-]`. (c) FileSystem.getInfoAsync verifies existence BEFORE calling Sharing.shareAsync — throws early on missing file. (d) Sharing.shareAsync called with mimeType='application/pdf' AND UTI='com.adobe.pdf'. (e) dialogTitle=composeQuoteWhatsAppMessage(...) so the caption hint shows on Android. (f) Web path unchanged: window.open(pdfUri) + window.open(wa.me/…?text=…). FileSystem import audit across the 5 required files ALL use 'expo-file-system/legacy' (grep confirmed: whatsapp.ts:3, pdf-merge.ts:2, app/(tabs)/index.tsx:18, app/preview.tsx:16, app/(tabs)/history.tsx:17); a full grep of /app/frontend/src and /app/frontend/app returned ZERO occurrences of the top-level 'expo-file-system' import. pdf-lib 1.17.1 is listed in package.json and installed in node_modules. Ek Dosyalar UI wiring verified in index.tsx: pickAttachments uses expo-document-picker with type=['application/pdf','image/*','application/msword','.docx MIME'], multiple=true, copyToCacheDirectory=true; Word files trigger toast 'Word dosyaları PDF'e otomatik eklenemez — atlanacak' and are filtered out of state; attachments render as rows (map at line 438) with a remove X (setAttachments filter at 451); resetForm (line 99) and loadFromQuote (line 92) BOTH call setAttachments([]). generatePdfUri (line 211) only invokes mergeAttachmentsIntoPdf when attachments.length>0 (line 226) and wraps it in try/catch that falls back to baseUri on error (line 230). pdf-merge.ts correctly branches PDF vs image (A4 letterbox at 595x842, 0.92 scale), skips Word, and on web returns a data: URI (native writes to cache). CRITICAL BLOCKER FOUND on web preview: page.goto(/) after authenticating throws Uncaught Error: `Cannot destructure property '__extends' of 'tslib.default' as it is undefined.` originating from node_modules/pdf-lib/node_modules/tslib/modules/index.js:3 (tslib 1.14.1 nested inside pdf-lib). Metro bundler resolves the tslib package.json 'exports.import' → './modules/index.js', which does `import tslib from '../tslib.js'; const { __extends, ... } = tslib.default;` — but the Metro-bundled CJS tslib.js does not expose a `.default` property that carries those helpers, so the destructure throws at module load. The error surfaces the moment ANY app code imports pdf-lib (pdf-merge.ts line 3 does `import { PDFDocument } from 'pdf-lib'` and is transitively pulled into (tabs)/index.tsx at line 27) — this crashes the ENTIRE expo-router bundle before the Teklif screen ever renders. Users on web cannot reach /(tabs) at all after auth; the red-screen LogBox modal is shown instead. This is a REGRESSION introduced by adding pdf-lib and is web-only (native builds through Hermes should not hit this path, but that cannot be verified from this environment). Deprecated packages detected: none new. Auth flow (register → PATCH /auth/me → POST /companies) still works via API — the crash is purely a Metro/web bundle issue.

react_native_issues.issue: Nested tslib 1.14.1 (node_modules/pdf-lib/node_modules/tslib) has an ESM 'exports.import' entry (modules/index.js) that is incompatible with Metro's CJS interop — it destructures `tslib.default.__extends` but the bundler-materialised default is undefined, throwing at module load. Reference: /app/frontend/src/lib/pdf-merge.ts:3 imports pdf-lib on all platforms. Suggested fix: add a top-level `resolutions` (or `overrides`) entry pinning `tslib` to `^2.6.2` in /app/frontend/package.json and reinstall (yarn install --check-files), OR conditionally require pdf-lib only on Platform.OS !== 'web', OR add a metro.config resolveRequest alias (protected file — prefer the resolutions path).

Note: the wordCount regex `/\.(docx?|)$/i.test(a.name)` has an empty alternation branch which will match ANY filename (the `|` before `)`); the additional `&& (a.mimeType || '').includes('word')` guard makes the toast fire correctly in practice but the regex is misleading. Consider `/\.docx?$/i` to make intent clear. Non-blocking.

pdf-lib is imported unconditionally at pdf-merge.ts:3, which means the web bundle eagerly evaluates it even when Platform.OS==='web' and we short-circuit to the base URI. This is what surfaces the tslib crash. Guarding the import (or the whole merge path) behind Platform.OS !== 'web' would eliminate the crash AND avoid shipping ~500KB of pdf-lib to web users who can't use native merging anyway.

rca_of_issue: RCA — pdf-lib/tslib Metro web crash: `pdf-lib@1.17.1` declares `tslib@^1.11.1` as a dependency; because the top-level /app/frontend/node_modules/tslib is a different major (2.x) it is NOT deduped, so Yarn installs a nested copy at /app/frontend/node_modules/pdf-lib/node_modules/tslib@1.14.1. tslib 1.14.1's package.json has `exports['.'].import = './modules/index.js'`. Metro's resolver honours the 'import' condition on web (and evaluates modules through its ESM-ish interop), so it loads modules/index.js whose source is `import tslib from '../tslib.js'; const { __extends, __assign, ... } = tslib.default;`. Metro compiles the parent tslib.js (which is a UMD/CJS bundle that assigns to `module.exports` — not ESM), and Metro's interop wraps it such that the destructured `tslib.default` is `undefined`. Result: TypeError at module load, before any of our app code runs, and the whole expo-router entry bundle aborts. Reproduction: authenticate and navigate to /, observe the LogBox red-screen with 'Cannot destructure property __extends of tslib.default as it is undefined' and a stack trace ending at node_modules/pdf-lib/node_modules/tslib/modules/index.js:3. Mitigation options (recommended order): (1) Add `resolutions: { "tslib": "^2.8.1" }` to /app/frontend/package.json and `yarn install` — forces tslib 2.x for pdf-lib and pdf-lib works fine with tslib 2.x helpers. (2) Or platform-gate the pdf-lib import in /app/frontend/src/lib/pdf-merge.ts so web never evaluates it: guard `mergeAttachmentsIntoPdf` with `if (Platform.OS === 'web') return basePdfUri` at the very top and switch `import { PDFDocument } from 'pdf-lib'` to a dynamic `await import('pdf-lib')` inside the native branch. (3) Or bump pdf-lib to a newer fork/release that pins tslib 2.x. Do NOT modify metro.config.js (protected). After applying, verify with a fresh page load that the Teklif tab renders and no '__extends' error is logged.
